facts.fact: RBI began operations on 1 April 1935 under the RBI Act, 1934.
RBI was nationalised on 1 January 1949.
RBI Central Board is appointed by GoI for four years; Governor + up to four Deputy Governors.
RBI is the sole issuer of notes; coins and the ₹1 note are issued by the Government.
As banker's bank RBI is the lender of last resort.
RBI manages forex reserves under FEMA.
The Hilton Young Commission (1926) recommended the RBI.
RBI began in Calcutta and moved its head office to Bombay in 1937.
The Banking Regulation Act, 1949 empowers RBI to regulate banks.
First RBI Governor: Osborne Smith; first Indian Governor: C.D. Deshmukh.
Sanjay Malhotra became the 26th RBI Governor on 11 December 2024.
Poonam Gupta is the RBI Deputy Governor in charge of monetary policy.
The RBI Governor is appointed by the Central Government and draws powers from the RBI Act (UPSC 2021).
RBI earns income from trading government bonds and foreign currency (UPSC 2025).
RBI promotes UPI and the Bharat Bill Payment System.
Repo rate is the rate at which RBI lends short-term to banks against government securities.
The LAF (repo/reverse repo) was introduced in 2000; OMO 1992; MSS 2004; MSF 2011.
SDF (2022) is the LAF floor and absorbs liquidity without collateral; MSF is the penal ceiling.
CRR is cash kept with RBI (no interest); SLR is liquid assets held by the bank itself.
As of Oct 2026: repo 5.50%, SDF 5.25%, MSF/Bank Rate 5.75%, CRR 3%, SLR 18%.
OMO sales and MSS issuance absorb excess liquidity from capital inflows.
The MPC was set up in 2016 under Section 45ZB of the RBI Act.
The MPC has six members: three from RBI (Governor chairs) and three external experts.
MPC meets at least four times a year; quorum four; Governor has the casting vote.
Inflation target: 4% CPI with ±2% band, reviewed every five years.
The MPC is chaired by the RBI Governor, not the Finance Minister (UPSC 2017).
Repo was held at 6.50% for 11 meetings (Feb 2023 – Dec 2024).
RBI cut repo by 125 bps during 2025 to 5.25% in December 2025.
RBI made a 50 bps repo cut in June 2025.
On 7 October 2026 the MPC raised repo by 25 bps to 5.50%.
The October 2026 stance became 'calibrated tightening'.
CRR was cut by 100 bps to 3% in phases from June 2025, releasing about ₹2.5 lakh crore.
RBI projected 2026-27 inflation at 5.2% and growth at 7.1%.
CPI inflation was 5.54% in September 2026.
Forex reserves were about $726 billion (9 Oct 2026).
In March 2026 the 4% (±2%) target was retained until March 2031.
A rise in Bank Rate indicates tight money policy (UPSC 2013).
OMO means RBI purchase and sale of government securities (UPSC 2013).
Sterilisation is done through OMOs (UPSC 2023).
A cut in SLR lets banks cut lending rates (UPSC 2015).
In an expansionary policy RBI would not raise the MSF rate (UPSC 2020).
Bank rate and OMO are monetary-policy components; public debt and revenue are not (UPSC 2015).
'MSF' and 'NDTL' are terms of banking operations (UPSC 2014).
Cost-push inflation comes from rising input costs; core inflation excludes food and fuel.
Creeping 1-5%, trotting 5-10%, galloping 10-20%, hyperinflation over 50% a month (source).
Demand-pull inflation is 'too much money chasing too few goods'.
Structural inflation stems from backward agriculture and inefficient distribution.
India's inflation peaked at 28.6% in 1974.
Quantity theory MV = PQ — Milton Friedman/monetarists; Keynes: liquidity trap.
CPI (NSO) has a new base 2024 with 358 items (from 299; old base 2012).
WPI (OEA, DPIIT) moved to base 2022-23 from 15 June 2026, with a new PPI.
CPI-IW is compiled by the Labour Bureau.
WPI excludes services; food has the highest CPI weight.
CPI is compiled by NSO and WPI by the Office of the Economic Adviser.
M0 reserve money; M1 narrow; M3 broad money (M1 + time deposits).
Money multiplier = 1/reserve ratio; RR 20% gives 5.
Multiplier is inversely related to reserve ratio; cash leakage lowers it.
Barter needs a double coincidence of wants.
Money: medium of exchange, unit of account, store of value, standard of deferred payment.
Fiat money is legal tender; fiduciary money rests on trust (cheques).
Reserve money is high-powered money.
M2 = M1 + post office savings; M4 = M3 + all post office deposits.
Liquidity order: currency > demand deposits > savings > time deposits (UPSC 2013).
The money multiplier increases with the banking habit of people (UPSC 2021).
Scheduled banks are in the Second Schedule of the RBI Act; RRBs are scheduled commercial banks.
Payments banks take deposits but cannot lend or issue credit cards (UPSC 2016).
14 banks nationalised in 1969, 6 in 1980; 2020 merger cut 10 PSBs to 4.
SARFAESI 2002 enables recovery of secured loans without courts.
PCA imposes RBI restrictions on weak banks.
PSL target is 40% of adjusted net bank credit.
MCLR (2016) replaced the base rate; new loans use an external benchmark.
Bank of Hindustan (1770, Calcutta) was the first bank; General Bank of India 1786.
Presidency Banks → Imperial Bank (1921) → SBI (1 July 1955).
Punjab National Bank (1894) was the first bank wholly managed by Indians.
Andhra Bank was founded in 1923 at Machilipatnam by Pattabhi Sitaramayya.
Andhra Bank merged into Union Bank of India on 1 April 2020.
Bank nationalisation dates: 19 July 1969 and 15 April 1980.
Dena and Vijaya Banks merged into Bank of Baroda (1 April 2019); 12 PSBs remain.
Narasimham Committees: 1991 and 1998.
Raghuram Rajan Committee on financial sector reforms: 2008.
Nachiket Mor Committee (2013) recommended payments and small finance banks.
P.J. Nayak Committee (2014) led to the Banks Board Bureau (2016), now FSIB.
Urjit Patel Committee (2014) recommended flexible inflation targeting.
First RRB: Prathama Bank, Moradabad, 2 October 1975; RRB Act 1976.
RRB shareholding: Centre 50, sponsor bank 35, State 15.
'One State, One RRB' (1 May 2025) cut RRBs from 43 to 28.
In AP four RRBs merged into the Andhra Pradesh Grameena Bank.
Minimum CRAR is 9% in India (Basel III 8%) plus 2.5% conservation buffer.
Small finance banks must give 75% of credit to priority sectors.
Payments banks may hold deposits up to ₹2 lakh per customer.
DICGC insures deposits up to ₹5 lakh.
An NPA is a loan overdue for more than 90 days.
NARCL (bad bank) was set up in 2021.
The external benchmark (EBLR) applies from 1 October 2019.
The June 2026 FSR expects bank bad loans below 2% through 2028.
Banking Laws (Amendment) Act, 2025 allows four nominees from 1 November 2025.
UCBs came under the BR Act in 1966; 2020 amendment tightened RBI supervision.
PMJDY began on 28 August 2014 (JAM trinity).
RRBs and Land Development Banks give direct credit; NABARD refinances (UPSC 2013).
Money market = ≤1 year instruments; capital market = long-term equity/debt.
Primary market issues new securities (IPOs); secondary market trades existing ones.
SEBI (1992 statutory) regulates securities.
IRDAI regulates insurance; PFRDA regulates NPS and APY.
Treasury bills are 91-, 182- and 364-day bills sold at a discount.
Commercial paper is an unsecured promissory note issued by companies (UPSC 2020).
Certificates of deposit are issued by banks.
Call money is overnight inter-bank lending.
TREPS replaced CBLO in 2018.
Only the government bond market and stock market are capital markets (UPSC 2023).
SEBI was set up on 12 April 1988; chair Tuhin Kanta Pandey.
The Forward Markets Commission merged with SEBI in 2015.
BSE (1875) is Asia's oldest exchange; NSE 1992; Sensex 30, Nifty 50.
Credit rating agencies are regulated by SEBI.
LIC 1956; New India Assurance 1919; GIC Re national reinsurer; IRDAI HQ Hyderabad.
NPS began on 1 January 2004; PFRDA Act 2013.
UPS from 1 April 2025: 50% of last-12-month average basic pay; Government contribution 18.5%.
Insurance penetration is about 4% against a world average of about 7%.
PMJDY drives financial inclusion via the JAM trinity.
NPCI (2008) runs RuPay, IMPS, UPI and BBPS.
RTGS (≥ ₹2 lakh) and NEFT are RBI systems, both 24x7.
UPI was launched in 2016.
e-RUPI (2021) is a prepaid purpose-specific voucher.
Digital Rupee pilots began in 2022 (wholesale 1 Nov, retail 1 Dec).
UPI is linked with Singapore's PayNow and accepted in UAE, France and elsewhere.
UPI processed 24.07 billion transactions worth ₹29.37 lakh crore in September 2026.
